items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Today one of the greatest trumpet players alive to me is Clark Terry.

ctx.x: I'd go into clubs like the Metro in New York to say hello and Charlie had a quartet there, and several other places, and I would listen to him and he would have me over for barbecue occasionally, and we were in close touch until his death. His death was premature. He had had many illness including diabetes, he wouldn't stop drinking or taking doctor's orders. I don't think Charlie was given full evaluation of his warmth and his beauty, because he had intertwined a great deal of technique in his jazz performances,…

Today one of the greatest trumpet players alive to me is Clark Terry. He's accepted as such, and I don't think critics of musicians put him down for his great technical prowress and swinging. Maybe Charlie didn't live long enough to enjoy the fulfillment and acceptance of his greatness, along his technical lines and
so forth -- as people admire that today, too, along with a person's swinging.
